person.name: Ali Ashrafzadeh
person.text: Joined Electra as **VP Clinical Development in June 2026** — only five months ago, which explains “no time for a change” right now. Before that: **Eli Lilly** for 6 years (Associate VP Medical, Immunology Research; Senior Medical Director) and **IQVIA** for 9 years (Medical Director, Therapeutic Strategy Lead and Chair of the Rheumatology Center of Excellence). Based in Rancho Santa Fe, California. Having spent 9 years inside a CRO, he knows exactly how outsourced biometrics should work — and where it breaks. Education: BS Biomedical Engineering and MA Medical Sciences (Boston University), MD (Ross University), internal medicine residency (Cornell-affiliated New York Methodist), rheumatology fellowship (University of Arizona). 1,986 LinkedIn followers.

company.text: Electra was spun out of **Star Therapeutics** in 2022 and is based in South San Francisco. It targets signal regulatory proteins (SIRPs), cell-surface receptors on activated immune cells, to deplete disease-driving cells while sparing normal immune function. Its lead antibody **ipsoprubart (ELA026)** is in a global registrational program for secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, a hyperinflammatory syndrome with no broadly approved therapy.

financials.text: Raised a **$183M Series C** in October 2025 (led by Nextech and EQT Life Sciences). Priced an upsized **$350M IPO** (23.3M shares at $15) on Nasdaq under **ETRA**, trading from Sep 18, 2026; underwriters hold an option for 3.5M more shares (up to ~$52.5M). Quarterly filings will now be public on SEC EDGAR.

history.text: LinkedIn, mid-October 2026. Ali: “at this moment we are actively working on our projects and there is no time for a change… perhaps in six months time.” Dmitri thanked him, offered help and asked for his email; Ali replied with **aliash.md@gmail.com**. The box was moved to *For Later Stage* on Oct 20.

industry.title: IPO window for late-stage immunology
industry.text: Electra's upsized IPO shows investors funding late-stage immunology assets with near-term registrational data. Companies in this position typically expand outsourced biometrics as they approach submission.

talking_points: How is the registrational sHLH program progressing, and when do you expect top-line data?
Who handles biostatistics and statistical programming today — in-house, a full-service CRO, or a niche provider?
Where do you feel the most time pressure between data management, programming and statistics?
Is ELA822 moving into the clinic, and will it use the same vendors?
Would a short submission-readiness review (SDTM/ADaM, ISS/ISE) be useful ahead of filing?
